subject: biology

hotspots.label: Root system
hotspots.description: The branching network of roots that grows downward into the soil, anchoring the plant and absorbing water and minerals.
hotspots.positionHint: The full root mass in the center of the scene, soil parted away.
hotspots.function: Anchors the plant and absorbs water and minerals.

hotspots.label: Root cap
hotspots.description: A protective covering at the very tip of the root that shields the growing tip as it pushes through soil.
hotspots.positionHint: Small rounded cap at the lowest point of the root tip.
hotspots.function: Protects the growing tip as it pushes through soil.

hotspots.label: Root hairs
hotspots.description: Tiny finger-like extensions just behind the root tip that greatly increase the surface area for absorbing water.
hotspots.positionHint: Fine short hairs clustering just behind the tip of the main root.
hotspots.function: Boost surface area so the root can soak up more water.

hotspots.label: Xylem tubes
hotspots.description: The inner water-conducting tubes that carry water upward, from the root into the stem.
hotspots.positionHint: Core of the root visible with the outer tissue layer toggled off.
hotspots.function: Carries water upward from the root into the stem.

hotspots.label: Food storage
hotspots.description: Many roots store extra sugar and starch as a food reserve, like carrots and potatoes.
hotspots.positionHint: Thickened swell on the root with a storage layer cloud toggled on.
hotspots.function: Stores sugar and starch as a food reserve.

visualStyleNotes: Anatomy Atelier bar throughout: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no scene props. A clean stylized diorama - muted warm soil browns and calm greens, not cartoon, not cluttered, no glow. Strong saturated color reserved for the flat hotspot dots.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0, matte roughness ~0.5-0.65. No emissive anywhere.
assetBrief: SUBJECT: an underground root system diorama with the soil parted away to reveal the full root mass. A central taper root with side branches, a protective root cap at the tip, fine root hairs behind the tip, an inner xylem tube revealed by an open scaffold, and a few thickened storage swellings. Warm tonal petals, muted greens and cream-browns. Named nodes: RootSystem, RootTip, RootCap, RootHairs, XylemInner, StorageSwell. Budget 10-14k.
